slug: 2020-01-01 People's Perspectives on ID and Civil Registration in Rwanda (World Bank)

facts.fact: The World Bank report states that since 2016 civil registration is done through NIDA, which receives birth and death data electronically so that a record is created or flagged in the National Population Register; registration itself takes place at the civil registrar offices at Sector level, and the report does not say where the data are entered (state at publication, 2020).
facts.system: Civil registration through NIDA into the National Population Register

facts.fact: The report states that the National Identification Agency (NIDA) is the permanent agency in charge of both the national ID and civil registration, and that the official authority for birth registration is the Ministry of Local Government (MINALOC) through its Directorate General of Territorial Administration and Good Governance (no date given; published 2020).
facts.system: Civil registration through NIDA into the National Population Register

facts.fact: The report states that a new digital birth registration system, letting a birth be registered paperlessly at the health centre or the Cell office with a NIN issued to the child, was 'about to be rolled out' and that NIDA was 'in the process of launching' it; at publication (2020) birth registration still took place at the Sector offices (416 Sectors, 2,148 Cells).

systems.tiers: Planned for health centres and hospitals (the Head Nurse completes the registration) and Cell offices; not yet rolled out at publication

systems.system: Civil registration through NIDA into the National Population Register
systems.tiers: Registered at civil registrar offices at Sector level and at embassies; birth and death data received electronically by NIDA since 2016
National; launched 2008, said to hold about 98 percent of the population

systems.system: National ID card and National Identification Number (NIN)
systems.tiers: Enrolment at Sector offices equipped with biometric data collection kits; refugee IDs also issued
Web portal and agents; all three birth certificate types paid for and obtained through it as of publication
Countrywide campaign in 2017 for birth registration, including late registration at no cost

note: Read from the artefact PDF. A qualitative study (fieldwork November 2019 to January 2020, 313 participants) on attitudes to the ID, birth registration and birth certificates; it gives no count of offices entering digitally and describes the digital birth registration system only as planned.
